highlights: Fall sowing windows for frost-hardy crops — kale, spinach, lettuce, chard, carrots, leeks and the rest — are now worked out from when growth actually stops in early November, not from the first frost date. Frost does not kill these crops, so first frost was never the thing that ended their season
Several packets that said "Sowing window passed for 2026" are sowable again as a result — on today's date that includes both lettuces and two spinaches
Crops that frost DOES kill are completely unaffected — their windows still close against the frost date, and nothing about them moved
